newsitem.title: USA: Texas spot electricity rebounds on higher natgas.
newsitem.headline: Texas spot electricity rebounds on higher natgas.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) rebounded Friday from recent weakness in tandem with a rise in natural gas futures.
Although spot power values in Texas were pegged higher with the rally in gas futures, actual cash trades were light due to lackluster demand, market sources said.

ERCOT firm, peak power for a 16-hour block for Monday was offered in a $25.00-$30.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) range, up from Thursday's $20.00-$22.00 for Friday. There was talk of distressed Monday deals near $15.00.
ERCOT electricity for non-firm delivery during Monday's heavy load hours was notationally assessed at $23.00-$29.00, up from $18.00-$19.00 Thursday.
Firm off-peak ERCOT deliveries for Monday were valued near $20.00, up from Thursday's $9.00-$11.00. There were reportedly distressed offers as low as $5.00 for Monday.
ERCOT electricity for non-firm delivery during Monday's light load hours stood at a notional area of $19.00, compared with $8.50-$10.50 Thursday.
ERCOT non-firm delivery over the five business days next week was quoted at $21.00.
Balance of January ERCOT electricity was assessed near $31.00, and February ERCOT power was valued at $27.00-$28.00.
Latest forecasts showed a weekend cool front would moderate temperatures in Texas to seasonal norms.

This week, the Lone Star state has enjoyed well-above normal temperatures with day readings mostly in the 70 degrees Fahrenheit range and night readings in the 40s-60s, some 20 degrees above seasonal norms.

On the New York Mercantile Exchange, February Henry Hub gas futures were up 17.0 cents at $3.060 per million British thermal unit (mmBtu). Swing gas prices in south Texas stayed in $2.30 area, near unchanged from Thursday.
